title: What changed in practice

segments.voice: Yesterday: what surprised you, Musa, a boat and a wall. Your line was surprised.

Good, or silent. Tie it, trust Him. Count before you are counted. The right hand, the name. Plant it anyway. Start next door. All year the lessons have ended with a short line and one small thing to try. A line like that can be said once and drift off with the day. That's how lines work. But maybe one didn't. Maybe a bismillah before meals is still there. Maybe a pause before speaking, or a coin set aside each week, or a quick check of the heart before sleep. Today, the habit that stuck.
screen: `GOOD, OR SILENT. TIE IT, TRUST HIM.` → `A LINE CAN DRIFT OFF.` → `ONE MAY HAVE STUCK.`

segments.voice: A hadith the year met at the charity jar: in Sahih al-Bukhari, Aisha reports, in paraphrase, that the Prophet, peace be upon him, was asked which deeds are most beloved to Allah, and he said: the most constant of them, even if they are small. Not the biggest. Not the most dramatic. The ones that keep going. How he lived it: asked whether he set aside special days for extra worship, Aisha answered, in paraphrase, that his deeds were constant, like steady rain, and that none of them could do what he did. Why small and constant? The year kept circling back to it. The boy at the platter got three short instructions and kept them for life. The Muwatta's line on character, the hadith on the heart, the tied camel: all practices for an ordinary Tuesday, not a once-a-year push. The habits the year asked for were small enough to survive a bad day. And if nothing stuck? The hadith doesn't ask for a list. It asks for one thing, kept. And the Qur'an tells those who have wronged themselves, in paraphrase, not to despair of Allah's mercy. Muslims call coming back tawbah, one of the stations the year studied: turning, and beginning again. So whatever stuck, or didn't, tomorrow's question is the same. What is one small thing, and will it still be there when the day is hard?
screen: `THE MOST CONSTANT, EVEN IF SMALL.` · `HIS DEEDS WERE LIKE STEADY RAIN.` · `SMALL ENOUGH TO SURVIVE A BAD DAY.` · `IF NOTHING STUCK, BEGIN AGAIN.`

segments.voice: Look back over the year for one habit still with you, however small, and be glad of it; if you don't find one, choose one now from the year's lines, small enough to keep. Picture the exact moment it will happen tomorrow, the kettle, the doorway, the first bite, the last light, and see yourself doing it there. If a heavier kind of despair comes and stays, please don't carry it alone: in the US, call or text 988, any hour, or elsewhere, local emergency help.
What changed in practice. The one habit from the year that kept going, small and constant, the kind the hadith calls most beloved. Today's word.
Your line: it stuck. Small and constant, the way steady rain keeps falling. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslim teachers encourage small, regular acts over occasional big ones, such as a fixed daily portion of Qur'an, a set extra prayer, or a regular charity, citing the hadith that the most beloved deeds are the most constant, even if small.
